_comment: Headless import corpus for the in-tree drawing fixtures (06-01).
profile paths are relative to <testfiles_dir>; absolute profile paths are
used as they are. Numbers are hand-derived from the fixtures: the drawing
is one A4 page (8.2677 x 11.6929 in, viewBox 0 0 595.2756 841.8898) with
seven flat fills per page, and every page of the derived three-page copy is
the same page record, so its paints and pixels repeat.
'derived:multipage-3' means: rebuild cdr_draw2.cdr at test time with three
drawing pages (the page record is duplicated inside the compressed drawing
stream and the source-path credit strings are neutralised).

plain-single._comment: one page, no output profile set: no pages, no icc-colour, the sRGB drawing; the page is painted (a thin-line A4 drawing covers about 3% of the canvas at 96 dpi).

cmyk-single._comment: the preferred output profile is attached on open and every flat paint is converted: seven fills, all icc-color, one profile element, the same paint count as the profile-less baseline; the on-screen pixels may move by at most 24/255 per channel.

multipage._comment: three drawing pages: three pages of the same A4 size, one top-level Page N layer each, identical duplicated content (page exports may differ only by antialiasing noise) and three PDF page objects.

multipage-cmyk._comment: three identical pages with the preferred output profile: three page elements and 3 x 7 flat paints, all of them icc-color of that profile.

dead-argv._comment: a container the parser cannot read: the command line converter fails with exit code 1, keeps the existing stderr lines and writes no output. The parser noise on stderr is expected for this fixture only.

dead-action._comment: the file-open action keeps the action convention: stderr and exit code 0, the previously active document stays active and is what gets exported.

profile-missing._comment: a preferred profile file that does not exist is ignored silently, exactly like a new document ignores it: the drawing stays sRGB.

stderr_contains: is not a valid ICC profile
allow_warnings: is not a valid ICC profile
profile-invalid._comment: an existing file that is not an ICC profile is reported once with the new-document wording and ignored: exit code 0 and no colour is converted.

e2e-seed._comment: 06-02 seed: the drawing opens with the preferred CMYK output profile and the capypdf export carries that colour — its content paints through the embedded 4-component ICCBased colour space (or four-operand k/K), so 'converted CMYK reaches the PDF'. Without the profile the paints stay sRGB and the pdf stage fails (the deliberate negative self-test), which is why this scenario has no svg/png expectations of its own.
